newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end higher, banking stocks in demand.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end higher, banking stocks in demand.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed higher led by strong demand in banking stocks and selective foreign buying of blue chips, dealers said.
"Banking stocks were in the limelight today. Buying was seen from both institutional and retail players," said one institutional dealer.
Analysts said recent merger plans among banks and expectations of more mergers this year have made banking stocks a favourite with punters.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks ended up 9.38 points or 0.76 percent to 1,241.87.
Malayan Banking led the rise in banking stocks, up 75 cents to 27.50 ringgit. The bank said it is releasing its half year results on Saturday.
Arab-Malaysian Merchant Bank, Kwong Yik Bank, DCB Holdings and Pacific Bank rose between 10 and 60 cents each.
Secondary stocks were kept firm by rotational interest though profit-taking was evident throughout the day.
The small-cap Second Board index ended 6.17 points or 1.01 percent higher at 614.54.
Telekom Malaysia firmed 40 cents to 20.80 ringgit, extending its recovery from recent sell-off.
